 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Rekha Palli
 Order

The present appeal preferred by the Insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act assails the award dated 29.01.2018 passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal insofar as it relates to the compensation awarded on account of the death of Ms.Ritu, a nine years old minor child.
Vide the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has dealt with three claim petitions in respect of three persons, who expired in the same fateful accident on 13.12.2016.

As the appellant/insurance company has preferred three separate appeals in respect of all the three claims, the present appeal is confined only to the compensation awarded on account of the death of Ritu, who lost her life in the fateful accident along with both her parents.

2. Vide the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.3,39,880/-
towards pecuniary loss of estate and an equivalent amount towards non-pecuniary losses.
Being aggrieved thereby, the present appeal has been filed by the insurer.

3. In support of the appeal, Mr.Gaur, learned counsel for the appellant has raised four grounds, his first contention being that no eye-witness to prove that the driver of the offending truck was driving rashly and negligently having been examined by the claimants, no finding of rash and negligent driving by the driver of insured vehicle could have been given.

He next submits and there being four pillion riders, along with the deceased on the motor-cycle at the time of the accident, it was evident National Insurance Co Ltd vs Master Shaurya & Ors on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43236623/
1 that the deceased had himself violated traffic rules and therefore no compensation was payable by the appellant.
4.

sentences.text: The third submission of Mr.Gaur is that the award of a sum of Rs.3,39,880/- towards non-pecuniary losses by the learned Tribunal was wholly unwarranted for which he places reliance on the decision of the Apex Court in Rajender Singh v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

entities.text: Rajender Singh v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [Civil Appeal No.2625/2020]
. He, therefore, prays that the amount towards non-pecuniary heads be reduced to Rs.2,25,000/-.
5. His final submission is that the learned Tribunal has also erred in awarding interest at the exorbitant rate of 9% per annum.
He, therefore, prays that the interest be reduced to 6% per annum.

He, however, submits that since this Court has already reserved orders in respect of the rate of interest qua the impugned award by way of MAC APP.526/2018 for orders, hearing on this aspect may be deferred for the present.
6.
However, learned counsel for the respondent prays for time to make submissions.

7. List on 25.04.2023.
